evals.query: I'm brand new to Kora and to compile-time DI frameworks. Teach me from scratch.
expected_behavior: Assesses the learner's Java/Kotlin and framework background before diving in
Ensures .kora-agent/ docs and examples are present, cloning them if missing
Starts from the getting-started guide and its guide app rather than an arbitrary topic
Explains concepts strictly from official sources following the Guides -> Documentation -> Guide apps -> Example apps hierarchy
Does not invent explanations and does not teach Kora through Spring/Micronaut analogies

evals.query: Explain how @KoraApp and Module interfaces build the application graph.
expected_behavior: Grounds the explanation in the official documentation/guides under .kora-agent/kora-docs
Explains the compile-time DI model (generated graph, no reflection) accurately
Points the learner at the relevant guide app or example app to see it in context
If a detail is not in the sources, says so instead of inventing it, and does not use other-framework analogies

evals.query: Walk me through building a first HTTP server endpoint in Kora, explaining every line.
expected_behavior: Follows the http-server guide and the corresponding guide app step by step
Explains each annotation (@Component, @HttpController, @HttpRoute) as it is introduced
Has the learner compile with ./gradlew clean classes to see the compile-time generation validate the code
Stays within documented Kora patterns and does not hand-wave behavior not shown in the sources
